title: 空乘岗位咨询 · 9月机经 Part 1
sourceNature: Ieltsa站方标为2026年9月的考生回忆重建；具体考场日期未独立核实，属于非官方IELTS资料，不能据此认定为官方原题。配套音频为站方重制录音，非已核实官方原声；中文精读由助手编写
instructions: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer. 从音频开头听起，完成第1–10题；听到Part 2后暂停。
contextParagraphs: Ellie向老同学询问空乘工作。笔记中已给出的其他信息：职责包括安全演示和提供食物；申请表可在公司网站下载；经历栏还包括在超市处理顾客询问。

questions.prompt: Duties include: some responsibility for _________ from sales during the flight.
Requirements: must be over age 19 and at least _________ cm tall.
Requirements: basic academic requirements: English and _________.
Requirements: at least one other _________ is desirable.
Training will include: what to do in case of _________ during a flight.
Training will include: awareness of different _________.
Application: mention experience of working in a _________ (voluntary work).
Other information: You don't have to buy a _________.

answers.explanation: The answer is 'money' because the speaker says, 'you'd be dealing with money... You'd be responsible for that' when talking about selling things during the flight.
The answer is '168' because the requirement is 'a minimum height. That's one hundred and sixty-eight centimeters.'
The answer is 'maths' because the speaker says, 'You need to show that you have a good level of English... and also maths.'
The answer is 'language' because the speaker says, 'it's an advantage if you can speak another language, although for cabin crew it's not essential.'
The answer is 'swim' because the speaker asks, 'can you swim?... that's another requirement.'
The answer is 'illness' because the training covers 'what action to take if a passenger suddenly has some sort of illness while you're in the air.'
The answer is 'cultures' because the training includes 'becoming aware of the variety of cultures that your passengers may come from.'
The answer is 'Eurontas' because the speaker says, 'It's a small airline called Eurontas. That's E-U-R-O-N-T-A-S.'
The answer is 'team' because the voluntary work was 'as part of a team,' and the friend says, 'that's something else they'll be looking for, being able to work with others.'
The answer is 'uniform' because the speaker says, 'the good thing about this airline is that they provide it for you,' meaning you don't have to buy it.

transcript:
PART 1

Part one.

You will hear two former school friends discussing a job as a cabin crew attendant. First, you have some time to look at questions one to five.

Now listen carefully and answer questions one to five. Hello? Oh, hello.

Um, this is Ellie Fisher. We were at school together. Oh, hi, Ellie.

How are you? What are you doing these days? Well, actually, I'm looking for a job, and I was wondering about applying to an airline, you know, looking after the passengers, and I heard you're doing something like that.

Yeah, I'm working as a cabin crew attendant. Right. So what does that involve?

Well, you might have to give them the initial safety demonstration before takeoff, for example. You've probably seen that when you've made a journey by air. Actually, I've never flown, but I'd love to.

That's why I'd like a job with an airline. Oh, right, and during the flight, you'd also be going round to see if anyone wants to buy anything. So I'd be dealing with money?

That's right. You'd be responsible for that, and then, of course, you'd be serving meals and snacks and things. Okay.

So can anyone apply? Well there are certain requirements. You must be at least nineteen years old, and there's also a minimum height.

That's one hundred and sixty-eight centimeters. That's to make sure you can reach the higher cupboards in the plane. Right.

I'm one hundred and sixty-nine centimeters, I think. What about qualifications? You need to show that you have a good level of English, that's written and spoken, and also maths.

Okay. Well, I passed my exams in both those subjects, fortunately. Mm-hmm, and it's an advantage if you can speak another language, although for cabin crew it's not essential.

I can speak Spanish. I did that at school until I was sixteen. Excellent.

That'll be very useful. And I'm pretty fit. I don't have any medical problems.

Okay. Oh, and can you swim? Yes.

Good, because that's another requirement.

Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions six to ten on page two.

Now listen and answer questions six to ten. Now, if you're accepted, you'll get a six-week training course. Right.

So that'll cover all aspects of the job, all the basic things you need to know, and then some special things like what action to take if a passenger suddenly has some sort of illness while you're in the air, for example. Right. I suppose you can't always count on a doctor being on board.

No. And then you'll have to do a lot of work during the training on becoming aware of the variety of cultures that your passengers may come from and the implications of that. That's really interesting, actually.

Okay. Well, I'd definitely like to apply. Um, what airline do you actually work for?

It's a small airline called Eurontas. That's E-U-R-O-N-T-A-S. Is that Nor M in the middle?

N for November. Okay. They're good people to work for.

Have a look at their website. You can download the application form from there. Right.

I don't have much in the way of experience, though. Well, what have you done since leaving school? I worked in a supermarket for a bit on the information desk.

I was helping deal with queries from customers. Okay. Put that down.

That's one of the most important aspects of the job, in fact. Oh, right, and last year I also did some voluntary work as part of a team. Should I put that down too?

Of course. That's something else they'll be looking for, being able to work with others. Right.

And a lot of airlines expect you to pay for your own uniform, but the good thing about this airline is that they provide it for you. Great. Well, thanks so much, Greg.

I really appreciate...

That is the end of

section one.

You now have half a minute to check your answers.
closeReadingHtml:
这段对话说了什么

Ellie想申请空乘工作，向老同学Greg了解真实职责、申请条件和培训。她还没有坐过飞机，但这不影响她询问工作。对话后半段转向她已有的超市服务与志愿经历，最后确认这家航空公司提供制服。

三组容易混淆的信息

  • 空乘最低身高是168厘米；Ellie说自己169厘米。前者是岗位门槛，后者是个人情况。
  • 另一门语言是优势，原文用an advantage和not essential限定；游泳则被称为another requirement。可取条件和必需条件不同。
  • “很多公司让你自己买制服”是一般情况，but之后才是Greg所在公司的安排：公司提供制服。

值得带走的词块

  • be responsible for / deal with：前者强调负责，后者强调处理事务。这段中二者共同指向售卖商品后的钱款管理。
  • apply to an airline / apply for a job：to后接申请的机构，for后接职位；同样的申请动作，介词随对象变化。
  • count on a doctor being on board：count on表示指望、依赖；being on board说明医生恰好在飞机上，这种条件不能保证。
  • the implications of that：不同文化带来的实际影响，而不只是记住文化名称。
  • as part of a team：作为团队成员。Greg强调的价值是working with others，即合作经验。

读懂长句与指代

“You'd be responsible for that”中的that回指前面的钱款处理；后面“they provide it for you”中的it回指制服，不是表格或培训。

培训内容里的“what action to take if a passenger suddenly has some sort of illness while you're in the air”可以分成三层：要采取什么行动（what action to take），在什么条件下（if乘客生病），发生在什么时候（while飞行途中）。整句重点是应急处置，不是要求空乘当医生。

“although for cabin crew it's not essential”让步说明会第二语言有好处但不是必需。把这一句与前面的an advantage连起来读，才能保留说话人的条件限制。

回到原音

核对后可重听介绍岗位条件到制服安排这一段，留意Greg怎样用right、of course和but确认、补充或限制Ellie的理解。原文就在下方，可边听边回读。
